text:
Mark Scheifele tied Saturday's game against Vegas 3-3 and, with that goal, passed Dale Hawerchuk for the most goals in Jets history. The Jets lost 5-4 in a shootout, but the night belonged to the centre who has been here through all of it, and who is still producing on a top line with Kyle Connor, already at 18 goals.

This was supposed to be a harder season. Winnipeg traded Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey in a multi-player deal in October, and Stuart Skinner and Nico Daws have been minding the net since. Yet the Jets are 11-9-4 and 7-2-1 in their last ten, with 52% of the expected goals in that stretch (the quality of chances). Over the season they're at 48%, their points are about two ahead of what their play has earned, and our playoff odds sit at 27%.

The supporting cast has carried more than you'd think. Dawson Mercer has 6 points in his last 10 games and Morgan Barron 8 (on 4.1 expected, so that one is running hot). Josh Morrissey's first goal of the season was an overtime winner against the Islanders. Viggo Björck's line with Adam Lowry and Alex Iafallo has controlled play in a small 66-minute sample.

The power play generates 0.80 expected goals a game, but the penalty kill gives up 0.84, and the Scheifele line's chances against (3.30 per 60 at 5v5) are nearly as high as its chances for. What we would watch: the goaltending without its anchor.
